scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: super_spine_router_0 zebra
Mechanism: zebra is FRR's RIB/kernel-interface daemon. It was killed
  together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it, while
  bgpd keeps running: the BGP sessions to spine_router_0_0
  (172.16.0.1) and spine_router_0_1 (172.16.0.3) stay Established
  because bgpd owns its own TCP sessions. The failure is in the
  management/route-programming plane: zebra-owned CLI queries (route
  table, interface state) fail, and bgpd can no longer program new
  routes into the kernel. Forwarding continues on the kernel FIB that
  zebra had already installed (a SIGKILL leaves kernel routes in
  place), and in this size-s fabric the super-spine is not even on the
  pc_0_0 <-> pc_0_1 data path (that path is leaf -> spine -> leaf), so
  there is no user impact -- but the device would blackhole any future
  route change it needs zebra to program.
Localization: super_spine_router_0
Root cause: zebra not running on super_spine_router_0 (bgpd still up)
Fix: restart FRR on super_spine_router_0 (`service frr restart`) --
  the config persists in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart brings back
  zebra, watchfrr and bgpd cleanly.

Observable note: the kill uses the same watchfrr-first pattern as the
lab-verified bgpd kills on this fabric (nothing respawns the daemon).
With zebra dead but bgpd alive, `pgrep zebra` is empty while
`pgrep bgpd` still returns a process; zebra-owned vtysh queries (e.g.
the route table) error out while BGP state remains queryable from the
peers. An agent that describes this as "FRR is partially down /
zebra crashed on super_spine_router_0" has found the fault.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on super_spine_router_0. The persistent
/etc/frr/frr.conf restores zebra (and watchfrr) alongside bgpd; the
route-programming and CLI/telemetry plane recovers, and the BGP
sessions re-establish.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The zebra daemon on super_spine_router_0 has crashed and is no longer
running. Zebra is FRR's core routing manager: it owns the kernel
interface table and the Routing Information Base (RIB), and it is the
process that vtysh connects to for interface-state queries and
route-table lookups. With zebra dead, any tool that asks FRR for
interface state or routing-table entries receives a "zebra is not
running" / daemon-connection error — exactly what the nightly audit job
observes.

The failure is confirmed by three independent data points: (1) the
FRR service unit is marked inactive (dead); (2) PID 50 recorded in
/var/run/frr/zebra.pid no longer exists (kill -0 returns "No such
process"); and (3) vtysh on the device itself reports "zebra is not
running" for any interface query. The stale zebra.pid and zserv.api
socket files in /var/run/frr/ are artefacts left behind after the
crash.

The watchdog process (watchfrr) is also absent — its PID file is
zero-length and the process does not appear in the process table —
which is why zebra was not automatically restarted after the crash.

bgpd (PID 57) survived as an orphaned process and continues to
maintain its BGP TCP sessions with both spine routers, which is why
those sessions remain Established. The kernel Forwarding Information
Base was already populated before zebra died, so data-plane forwarding
between pc_0_0 and pc_0_1 is unaffected.

Root cause: zebra crashed on super_spine_router_0 and watchfrr is not
running to restart it, leaving the FRR management plane broken while
the data plane continues forwarding.

Corrective fix: run `systemctl restart frr` on super_spine_router_0.
This will cleanly restart zebra, watchfrr, and all other configured
FRR daemons, re-establishing the management plane and resuming normal
route-table and interface-state queries.
